issue: #1919 split-identity pool rows — the sport-segment class, tranche 2, RELOCATE
note: This file IS the scope. relocate-pool-rows-by-list.cjs touches exactly these ids and nothing else. Every entry was classified from the 2026-09-07 whole-corpus re-measurement (16,904,905 rows walked, READ ONLY) and BOTH of its candidate addresses were checked live against card_catalog with identityBackingOf. Part 6 of 6 of the RELOCATE class — split across files only to keep each list reviewable in a diff; each file is an independent scope. Rows already parked on 2026-09-07 are excluded.
rulings: CF-A-SPLIT-ROW-POLLUTES-TWO-POOLS. Re-measured over the whole corpus on 2026-09-07: the _ts plan covered all 16,904,905 rows in 152 bisected windows and 16,863,838 came back READ ONLY (the 41,067-row difference is live churn across the ~50-minute walk, not a skipped range: the planned chunk counts sum exactly to the corpus and the only boundary gaps are windows a COUNT proved empty). 101,250 rows carry a cardId whose SPORT segment differs from their hobbyiqCardId. 7,999 were parked on 2026-09-07 (#1919 lists 01-04) and are skipped here; 93,251 remain. The exact-pool reader ORs the two identity fields, so each such sale is read into TWO pools and prices a card it is not.

THE WRITE-TIME GUARD HOLDS, AND _ts DOES NOT PROVE IT ALONE. #1929 (prod 11794bc, deployed 2026-09-07T02:03:36Z) refuses a split row at the write door. 7,996 split rows carry a _ts at or after that deploy — but _ts is LAST-MODIFIED, not created, and all 7,996 of them are ids from the 2026-09-07 park apply, which patched those rows minutes after the deploy and bumped their _ts. Attributed by id, GENUINE NEW SPLIT ROWS SINCE THE GUARD: 0. This tranche therefore repairs a CLOSED population — stored rows only, with no live emitter behind it.

A DECIDABLE ROW IS NOT PARKED. PARK (identityUnverified) is the vehicle for a row whose right side the catalog cannot name. Where EXACTLY ONE of the two addresses carries a checklist-backed card_catalog row (identityBackingOf, the same predicate the pricing gate uses), that side IS the card and the row is REPOINTED or RELOCATED to it rather than parked — parking a decidable row throws away a sale we can place.

hobbyiqCardId IS NOT AUTOMATICALLY THE WINNER (#1924). Measured on same-setKey sport splits with an unambiguous setKey tell, hobbyiqCardId was correct 2,330 times and cardId 1,203 times. So neither field is preferred here: the CATALOG decides, per row, and a row on which the catalog is silent or speaks for both sides is parked.

A CHECKLIST-BACKED ADDRESS IS NOT AUTOMATICALLY THIS SALE'S ADDRESS. The first dry run routed an "Upper Deck Halo Legacy Collection Carter-A259 ... #51" sale to hiq:baseball:2024:bowman:51:base:no-auto because that address IS checklist-backed — by 2024 Bowman #51, a real and entirely different card that happens to share the number. Filing a Halo sale into a real baseball card's comp pool is the exact defect this repair exists to undo. So the SALE'S TITLE holds two VETOES over the catalog's winner and can elect neither side: the title must not name a different VERTICAL, and it must name a PRODUCT that corroborates the destination. A title that names no product carries no route.

A ROUTE NEEDS TWO REAL ADDRESSES. 902 rows the catalog was willing to route carry a side that is not a card address at all: "hiq:sight::be80caf8-…::bulk" and "hiq:hedge::1682403647139x…" are cardsight/cardhedge VENDOR KEYS with an "hiq:" prefix glued on, so their vertical segment is the tail of a vendor name; "hiq:ant::hiq:basketball:2025:…" is a slug prefixed onto another slug; and "hiq:baseball-mlb:…", "hiq:mlb-baseball:…", "hiq:hockey-ice-hockey:…", "hiq:other:…" name verticals absent from the shipped CANONICAL_SPORTS. None is a disagreement between two cards — each is a key defect and its own repair. Routing off one would launder a junk partition into a real card's pool while the banner read "RELOCATED", so they PARK with the defect named. Every routed row in this tranche has a well-formed hiq address with a canonical vertical on BOTH sides.

RELOCATE — the partition key is the wrong address. hobbyiqCardId carries a checklist-backed card_catalog row and cardId does not. sold_comps is partitioned on /cardId, so placing the sale on the card the checklist names is a new document plus a delete of the old, in that order, with a verified read between — relocateSoldComp (D19) owns the ordering. Both identity fields land on the destination: a move that carried only one half would leave the row in both pools, which is the defect itself.
